To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

factor analysis of pupillary test data revealed three pupillary test factors, that maximal pupillary area is a useful test parameter for investigation of pupillary function and that the pupillary light reaction is not impaired in patients with IDDM and NIDDM.

(a) factor analysis of the pupillary test parameters of normal subjects revealed three factors; (b) the three factors were also extracted from the pupillary test data of diabetic patients; and (c) from the comparison of the pupillary parameters of normal and diabetic groups, maximal pupillary diameter and latency time are the most sensitive pupillary parameters for investigation of diabetic patients.
the three pupillary parameters maximal pupillary area (M), contraction velocity (V1), and latency time (L) of pupillary light reaction (PLR) are suitable to investigate the PLR in diabetic patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an objective and reliable test of the pupillary autonomic system.
the development of a simple and reliable test for the investigation of autonomic pupillary function.
the development and validation of a method of pupillometry which is suitable for clinical use.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

pupillary function can be investigated by a simple test battery of two parameters, maximal area and latency time, and that these two parameters can be used to assess the pupillary light response in normal subjects as well as in diabetic subjects.
the pupillary light test is not a useful tool for investigating the pupility autonomic function in diabetics.
the maximal pupillary area is a useful parameter in diabetic patients for investigating pupillary autonomic neuropathy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pupillary light reflex is a useful tool for investigating the autonomic nervous system of diabetic patients, but it should be used with great care.
the pupillary light response can be assessed by two parameters, maximal pupil size and pupillary light reflex latency time, which can be measured easily and reliably in a short time.
pupillary autoregulation is not affected by diabetic autonomic neuropathy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pupil is a good indicator of autonomic function in diabetes and the pupil can be used as a noninvasive, inexpensive and easy to perform test to assess autonomic dysfunction in diabetic patients.
the pupillary light response is a very sensitive measure of autonomic neuropathy.

factor analysis is a valuable tool to investigate pupillary test data in diabetic subjects and that pupillary autoregulatory function in diabetic subjects can be assessed by two pupillary parameters, maximal pupil area and latency time of the pupillary response.
